drafts.title: Front seats with longer thigh support and rear legroom matching main competitors
drafts.description: Tall drivers can extend front seat cushion support and rear passengers get legroom at least as generous as the segment leaders so long journeys are comfortable for all occupants.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Front seat cushion fore-aft support depth (measured from seat back contact point to front cushion edge) >= 520 mm; ability to adjust effective thigh support by at least 60 mm. Rear knee room (heel-to-seat-back) >= 940 mm measured at standard seat position. Verified in vehicle packaging mock-ups and target demographic user tests with drivers >= 190 cm.
assumptions: Target values chosen from competitor benchmarking (assume main rivals average rear knee room ≈ 940 mm and current model front cushion depth ≈ 460–480 mm).
Measurements use standard OEM interior measurement procedure; adjustments via cushion geometry and seat track travel are feasible within successor architecture.
No change to occupant crash envelopes that would reduce safety; final dimensions will be refined in packaging engineering.
uncertainties: Final achievable fore-aft depth depends on seat mechanism packaging and side airbag integration.
Trade-offs with rear-seat thickness and center tunnel height may affect exact rear knee room.

drafts.title: Reliable exterior closures in cold and hands-free tailgate responsiveness
drafts.description: Exterior closures (hands-free tailgate and flush door handles) operate reliably across expected climates so owners don't need several attempts to open the tailgate or manually thaw door handles in freezing weather.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Hands-free tailgate opens on the first attempt in >=95% of test trials across temperature range -20°C to +40°C and common footwear/approach angles. Flush door handles operate (unlock and open) without manual thawing in >=98% of cycles at -20°C ambient and after 12 hours parked in freezing conditions.
assumptions: Tests performed with standard keyfob, typical user approach speeds and footwear; ice buildup simulated per climate lab protocol.
Hardware and sealing improvements are feasible within the successor vehicle timeline.
Acceptable failure rates correspond to typical field reliability targets for luxury segment closures.
uncertainties: Extreme owner modifications (heavy ice accumulation beyond lab protocol) may still cause failures.
Software/hardware interactions (e.g., sensor misreads due to ice) could require iteration after initial release.

drafts.title: Seat memory that reliably restores saved positions
drafts.description: When occupants recall a saved seat position, the seat returns to the saved position consistently so drivers do not need to fine-adjust after recall.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Memory seat recall restores driver seat position to within ±10 mm translationally and ±1° rotationally of the saved position in >=98% of recall attempts, measured after vehicle unlock/start and after rear-seat fold events.
assumptions: Measurement follows a repeatable seat-position measurement protocol (reference points on seat and pedal).
Software debouncing and position sensors are tuned to avoid drift between saves and recalls.
uncertainties: High wear or mechanical play late in vehicle life may degrade precision; warranty and calibration strategy may be needed.

drafts.title: Cup holders sized for common bottles and secure retention under normal maneuvers
drafts.description: Cup holders accept common consumer bottles and travel mugs and hold them securely to avoid tipping or spillage during routine driving.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Cup holders accommodate bottles up to 85 mm diameter and up to 300 mm height; a held bottle must not tip over in lateral acceleration events up to 0.4 g in standardized lane-change tests.
assumptions: 85 mm diameter covers large bottled water and many insulated travel mugs; 0.4 g lateral acceleration represents aggressive cornering maneuvers.
Retention achieved by geometry and soft inserts rather than introducing fragile mechanical clamps.
uncertainties: Very wide aftermarket tumblers (>85 mm) will remain unsupported; multiple cup holder sizes may be necessary in some trim levels.

drafts.title: Expanded ambient lighting palette and brightness control with user presets
drafts.description: Interior ambient lighting offers a wide selection of colors and finer brightness steps so customers can personalize cabin mood and save preferences.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: At least 64 selectable colors and a minimum of 10 brightness levels available across at least 6 lighting zones; users can save and recall at least 5 custom lighting presets.
assumptions: LED drivers and software allow 64-color generation (via color mixing) and 10 brightness steps without perceptible flicker.
6 zones provide meaningful differentiation (front doors, rear doors, dashboard, footwell, center console, rear parcel).
uncertainties: Perceived color accuracy may vary by material reflectivity; calibrations will be needed for different interior trim options.

drafts.title: Convenient 12 V accessory outlet in the trunk able to run a cooler box
drafts.description: Owners can power portable coolers or other accessories directly from a trunk socket without needing aftermarket adapters.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: A fused 12 V accessory outlet in the trunk capable of supplying at least 10 A continuous (≈120 W) with grounded connection and a covered weatherproof socket.
assumptions: 10 A continuous supports typical 12 V cooler boxes; vehicle electrical architecture provides the required fused circuit.
Socket placement is convenient for common cooler box placements and includes protection against accidental shorting.
uncertainties: Higher-power accessories (>10 A) will require higher-capacity circuits; safety and thermal management must be confirmed in vehicle integration.

drafts.title: Request for front end to meet new EU pedestrian protection regulation (logged)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the vehicle front end meets the new EU pedestrian protection regulation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Front end design complies with the new EU pedestrian protection regulation as required for homologation in applicable markets.
assumptions: Regulatory compliance and certification belong to legal/homologation workstreams and may require changes to exterior geometry and airbag systems.
uncertainties: Exact technical measures required will follow the published regulation text and homologation testing outcomes.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulation/homologation request — logged for compliance teams rather than a customer-facing product requirement.

drafts.title: Request for side windows with 4.5 mm laminated glass (engineering spec logged)
drafts.description: Customers requested 4.5 mm thick laminated side glass.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Side windows use 4.5 mm laminated glass per customer request (logged as engineering specification).
assumptions: Thicker laminated glass is an engineering/materials request; acoustic benefits and weight impact will be validated by NVH and structural teams.
uncertainties: Final glass thickness may vary by roofline or sunroof presence; integration may affect weight and center of gravity.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering material specification — out of scope for customer-facing requirement; logged for engineering teams.

drafts.title: Request for seat cushion foam density of 55 kg/m³ (engineering spec logged)
drafts.description: Customers requested seat cushion foam with density of 55 kg per cubic meter.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Seat cushion foam specified at 55 kg/m³ density per customer request (logged as material specification).
assumptions: Foam density is a materials engineering specification; comfort perception also depends on cell structure and layering.
uncertainties: Actual comfort may require different foam constructions despite matching density; durability vs comfort trade-offs to be validated.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering/material specification — logged for seating and materials teams.
